newsitem.title: UK: Total of UK inward investment projects hits record.
newsitem.headline: Total of UK inward investment projects hits record.

text.p: Britain attracted a record 483 direct inward investment projects in 1996/97, up from 477 in 1995/96, the Department of Trade and Industry said on Wednesday.
The projects created 46,179 jobs and safeguarded a further 47,545, Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett said in a statement.
She also announced a new investment -- an automotive components plant to be built by Canadian company Multimatics in the West Midlands, which will create 350 jobs.
"Britain is rightly proud of its record in attracting inward investment from around the world and we have good reason to be confident about the future," Beckett said.
She said Britain was a magnet for leading edge research and technological production, supported by a widening base of local suppliers.
"I want to ensure a climate in which inward investors can be assured of quality and added value by locating in Britain," she said.
Beckett said the key to many investment decisions had been the creation of partnerships between business, investment agencies, and local and national government.

"Our aim now is to ensure that attractive conditions are maintained and such partnerships developed further so that Britain can meet the very real challenges that lie ahead in competing for investment on the world stage," she said.
